content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends specific viral load (VL) thresholds to differentiate between treatment failure and undetectable levels. A viral load greater than 1000 copies/mL is indicative of treatment failure, while a viral load of 50 copies/mL or less is considered undetectable. 2. The numerator has been updated for clarity, but the calculation of the indicator and its measurement remain unchanged. 3. On page 75, Figure 3 should be replaced with the corrected version provided. 4. On page 309, line 23, the term HIV status (positive, negative) should be replaced with HIV status (positive, negative, unknown status). 5. On page 313, lines 17–33, the section Method of measurement for the numerator has been revised. Direct estimates from HIV case surveillance systems should only include individuals diagnosed with HIV, reported by a surveillance system, and still alive. Only confirmed HIV diagnoses should be counted, and mechanisms must be in place to remove duplicate reports of individuals from multiple facilities or reported multiple times. 6. For countries with robust case surveillance and vital registration systems, the number of people aware of their HIV status can be derived using the Case Surveillance and Vital Registration (CSAVR) fitting tool within the Spectrum AIDS Impact Module (AIM). 7. For the denominator, estimation models such as Spectrum AIM are the preferred source for determining the number of people living with HIV. In countries where household survey data is used to model estimates, separate estimates for children (0–14 years old) may need to be constructed using program data to produce an overall estimate for all ages. This approach represents the most conservative measure of knowledge of HIV status within the population. 8. On page 386, lines 23–24, the term Probable route of transmission has been updated. The revised list includes heterosexual sex, sex between men, unprotected intercourse during sex work, injecting drug use with unsterile equipment, nosocomial transmission, vertical transmission, and other routes. 9. On page 386, lines 26–27, the definition of Key populations has been updated. The revised definition includes men who have sex with men, people living in prisons and other closed settings, people who inject drugs, sex workers, transgender and gender-diverse individuals, as well as adolescent girls and young women. 10. These corrections have been incorporated into the electronic file.
